title: DFS and connected parts
objective: Count connected parts by diving as deep as possible (DFS) from each unvisited piece.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): depth-first search
Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: graph traversal

simplifies: The grid is tiny, so recursion depth is fine. On a huge grid the recursion could get too deep; the same idea works with an explicit stack.

quiz.prompt: Why does the scan count a new island only on unvisited land?

options.text: Each island is fully marked as soon as it is found, so any unmarked land must be a different island
options.explanation: Right. Sinking the whole island first is what keeps the count honest.
It is about marking, not rarity.
That would count cells, not islands.

quiz.prompt: Are two land cells that touch only at a corner the same island here?

options.explanation: Right. Only up, down, left and right count as touching in this lesson.
Diagonals aren't in STEPS here. Some problems include them, and then they would be.

options.text: Only if both are on the edge
options.explanation: Position doesn't matter; only the four directions do.
